paragraphs.text: A **cash-secured put** is a short put position in which the writer sets aside enough cash to buy the shares at the strike price if the put is assigned [S1]. The writer sells the put, collects the premium up front, and accepts the obligation to buy 100 shares per contract at the strike any time before expiration [S1]. In a cash account the broker holds the full purchase price as collateral for the whole life of the trade [S1]. The app also shows a **probability OTM**: the model's estimate of the chance that the option finishes out of the money at expiration and therefore expires worthless [S6]. If the put is exercised against the writer, **assignment** is the process by which an option writer is selected to fulfil the obligation of a contract that a holder has exercised [S2].

Buying power was split with a tilt of {{allocation.tilt}}: {{allocation.csp_pct|pct}} to cash-secured puts ({{allocation.csp_dollars|money}}) and the remainder in cash. The regime label was {{regime.label}}, with the VIX at {{regime.vix}} and a risk-free rate of {{regime.risk_free_rate_pct|pct}}.

The **VIX** measures the market's expectation of 30-day volatility in the S&P 500, quoted as an annualised percentage [S5]. It is computed from option prices rather than from past returns, so it moves with fear and relief in real time [S5].
